take: Oil markets are trading a narrow range as forecasts of a coming surplus collide with continued Middle East attacks and stalled diplomacy, whilst EIA data show collective oil flows through Middle East chokepoints rose 19% in 3Q26 — the physical barrels are still moving, which keeps prompt crude and freight honest even as paper bets on the glut. On the shipping side, it has been a bloody week in the Persian Gulf and around the Black Sea with little sign of peace, and a sanctioned Russian vessel was attacked by drones near Finland, so war-risk premia and rerouting remain the live transmission channel into tonne-miles and tanker rates. The positioning angle is that the surplus is still a forecast rather than an inventory fact, and with US crude imports from Venezuela at 701,000 b/d in July (655,000 b/d in August) and refineries shifted toward middle distillates on high distillate and jet margins, the product complex — not crude — carries the tighter fundamental. Watch the gasoil-to-bunker spread as the cross-market tell: distillate-led refinery yields support gasoil whilst any softening in HSFO on heavier OPEC+ flows would widen the Hi-5 and pull scrubber economics further apart. Over the next 24 hours, keep an eye on any escalation headlines out of the Gulf and Black Sea, the Asian tech sell-off spilling into broader risk appetite, and whether the surplus narrative finally shows up in visible stock builds rather than agency reports.
